**Prerequisite edge standing -> carry-over** (form **state**, gate carried_open_visits). `policy_source`: "The visits of a standing referral are fixed only after every single referral that an earlier assignment of the member issued and that is still within its validity is carried on the current assignment under its original referral number."
- Carried verbatim in doc_pcp_standing_referrals_b647f4d8, section "When its visits are fixed" (the blocked policy's hub). Connective "only after", strength hard, form state (what is waited on is a record state: an entry under the original number on the current assignment).
- Same-form restatements in the same document: "so long as any single referral issued under an earlier assignment … is not on the current assignment under its original referral number, the visits of a standing referral are not yet fixed" and the three-row table. No action or tool named.
- Resolution basis: the depended-on hub states the write in the same words ("is carried onto the member's current active assignment under its original referral number"); validity from referral terms (b)/(f) and the carry-over hub's "keeps its own expiry"; records = the earlier assignment's referral entries and the current assignment's history. Resolvable at the source's strength (confirmed in the blind audit, hop state-derived).
- Not carried in any other policy's document: no carry-over doc mentions a standing referral (scan: 0 occurrences of "standing referral" in the four carry-over-policy docs).
- `condition`, `resolved_by`, `effect` have no home in any document (checked: tool name `carry_over_referral_de0684af` appears only in the carry-over hub).

### Base policies governing the subjects

- `pcp_referrals` -> doc_pcp_specialist_referral_terms_c927336b: terms (a)–(f) carry every clause (referral required where the flag is true; validity days from issue date; single and standing ceilings; self-referral list; referral never replaces a prior authorization; issued only on an active assignment, "as the assignment's status stands on the system record before the referral is issued" = eligibility `referral_from_active_pcp`, system_record, pre_action; ended PCP's referral valid until its own expiry). Schedule matches every variant value (validity 180/180/180/180/365/365/365; single ceiling 6/6/6/6/12/12/12; standing allowed and ceiling 0/0/0/0/24/36/24; referral required Yes/Yes/No/Yes/Yes/No/Yes).
- `pcp_provider_exit` -> doc_pcp_provider_network_exit_fe901b39: notification by the later of lead days / after-receipt days (30/15 all types), postpartum continuity by type (Yes/No/Yes/Yes/Yes/No/Yes), reassignment effective the exit date with end reason provider left network — all in force and carried.
- **Retired surface**: `overwrite` of `pcp_ext_continuity_of_care` retires exactly "A member in active treatment may keep seeing the exiting provider for continuity_of_care_days after the exit date". The network-exit doc keeps that clause struck through with "**This clause is no longer in force.** It has been superseded by the current continuity-of-care basis for the continuity visits recorded on a continuity-of-care referral." — present, marked retired, not stated as in force; the policy's other clauses stay in force; no other clause is written as retired anywhere in the corpus. The `replaced_by` text is carried in doc_pcp_continuity_window_f8ae71a4.
- Variant parameters read by the three policies (continuity_of_care_days 90, referral_max_visits, standing_referral_max_visits, standing_referral_allowed, referral_validity_days) are all carried with their figures.
- Sweep of the other base policies (single active / multi-holding, practice match, panel capacity, distance standard, change limit, effective dates, auto-assignment, initial health appointment, dismissal, access standards, service features incl. the ID-card trigger from the `pcp_activate` event): every schedule value in the KB equals the variant parameters; no finding.

## kb_to_source

Sentence-by-sentence read of every normative claim in the 48 documents, with emphasis on the 17 documents of the three policies above:

- Every obligation, eligibility, calculation, window, order and tool statement has a structured source (rule text, factor ladder, baseline, compute, tool docstring or base rule/param). Derived restatements checked for equivalence: "Carrying a referral changes where the referral is listed, not when it runs out" (= keeps its own expiry); "The ceiling is applied before the deduction, never after it" (= source order); "A member with no earlier assignment, or whose earlier assignments' single referrals are all past their validity, has no such referral to wait on" (= vacuous case of the prerequisite); the continuity-rate table row "3 | 0 | 0 (current cadence)" (= method applied); medication-review row naming "covered over-the-counter" fills among the zero tier (inside the source's "any other member"). All entail nothing beyond the source.
- Worked examples re-computed (window boundaries, whole-month ages, 45-day and 61-day counts, 20 × 45 / 365 = 2.47, 5 legs -> 2, notification dates): all correct; all marked hypothetical.
- Added confirmations, reviews, notifications, waits or exception procedures: none found.
- Prerequisite-side specific checks: (1) cross-problem operational guidance ("if unmet, first call …"): none — each of the five task-tool names occurs only in its own hub (runtime grep over the whole published KB); (2) a task's opening world state written as a policy fact: none — every example is labelled hypothetical. A literal grep of the corpus for task 0's NPIs, referral numbers, assignment ids, member names, exit date and renewal date finds nothing. One date coincides: doc_pcp_claims_lookback_by_referral_age_33b14bf6's worked example "A referral issued 20 April 2026 is 4 whole months old on 15 September 2026, so the 6-month window applies", and task 0's carried referral RF-2604-58213 was also issued 2026-04-20. The example is explicitly hypothetical. It uses a different handling date (15 September, where it is 4 months old; at the task's 24 September it is 5 months old) and different claim dates (16 March, 2 July, 15 March 2026, 1 November 2025; none is a task-0 claim). It states no fact about any member, so it is not world state written as policy. See dependency_form for the tier question.
- Omissions or rewrites: none.

## bijection_verdict

**PASS.** Every normative atom of the three extended policies (including every factor tier, every baseline default and the untriggered branches — renewal-due alignment, recent-window look-back, four-or-more-legs travel method, maintenance rate, zero tiers), of `pcp_referrals` and `pcp_provider_exit`, and of the three tool contracts has an equivalent home; the retired clause is carried as retired; no claim lacks a source. First revision; no earlier revision exists.

Notes (not findings):
- N1. Several factor documents state their fall-back tier by the source's own name for the baseline quantity rather than by figure ("the standard standing allowance", "the standard continuity rate", "the standard referral visits", "the practice type's continuity-of-care days"). These are tier *values* equal to baseline defaults, not thresholds; the figure is stated in the computation document or the product schedule, so each tier still yields a definite number.
- N2. The prerequisite sentence of the continuity policy lives in a factor document (co-management) rather than the hub. This is within "its hub or one of its fragments"; findability was confirmed in the blind audit through the term "continuity-of-care referral".

Read of the whole pcp corpus against the blind answer's hop marks (both hops state-derived, none pre-solved):

- State-form sentences restated as actions: none. The co-management doc's restatements and heading ("Standing referral on the active assignment") name the state only; the standing hub's restatements and table name the record state ("on the current assignment under its original referral number") only.
- Another problem's tool named in a blocked problem's documents: none (tool names only in their own invocation blocks).
- A dependency or order between problems stated beyond the sentences, or a sentence carried in a second document: none. The standing baseline's "specialist named on the most recent single referral that the current assignment carries" and its deduction, and the co-management truth table's "Active assignment carries a standing referral", are the source's own computation law (rule / factor ladder), not dependency statements.
- Aggregated dependency tables, checklists, roadmaps or ordered cross-problem step lists: none.
- Wrong-vs-correct contrasts, named mistakes, cross-problem examples/FAQs: none.
- Titles or openings mirroring a task: none — titles name general subjects ("Continuity-of-Care Election", "Standing Referrals for Ongoing Conditions", "Carry-Over of Unexpired Specialist Referrals", "Co-Management Reduction for Care Shared with a Specialist", …); no title restates a caller's request.
- Depended-on documents reachable only through borrowed phrasing: no — the standing hub is reached by "standing referral"/"active assignment", the carry-over hub by "carried … under its original referral number", the words of the prerequisite sentences and of the records.
- Factor documents saying which tier customers fall on, or writing evidence rows as fact: none. Checked specifically: the claims look-back factor's hypothetical worked example uses an issue date (20 April 2026) that coincides with task 0's carried referral. It is framed as a hypothetical at a different handling date. It does not say that any customer is on a tier, and it writes none of task 0's evidence rows (the specialist claims it lists are not task 0's). A reader still has to compute the referral's age and count the claims from the records. Recorded as an observation, not a KB-EXPLICIT finding.
- Computation documents hinting at modification ("unless otherwise provided", "certain customers qualify", pointers): none. The words "standard" ("standard look-back window", "standard continuity rate", "standard standing allowance") are the source's own names for the baseline quantities. The continuity-window factor doc's phrase "in place of a fixed continuity-of-care period for every member in active treatment" is the verbatim `overwrite.replaced_by` text and refers to the retired base clause, not to the computation document or another factor. The network-exit doc's "superseded by the current continuity-of-care basis …" is the retired-surface marking and names no document, tool or route.

**PASS** (no KB-EXPLICIT finding).
